- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.4), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect risk reversal or market recovery.
- Model consistently underestimates prices after recent spikes (e.g., >72) — apply a “mean reversion” bias: if price >72, forecast next period = max(70, previous + 0.5×(spike - 70)).
- Model often lags sentiment shifts: if sentiment turns positive after 3–5 days, forecast should rise by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overpredicts early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days) — cap first 5 days’ forecast at 10% below true mean of last 18 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversals” (e.g., +0.4 → -0.2 → +0.6), model tends to misread momentum — apply a “sentiment momentum filter”: if sentiment flips within 3 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 2 days.
